headline: Saturday's wire split the Hormuz story into two tracks: Trump's claim of a Sunday signing — ‘the Hormuz Strait is OPEN TO ALL’ — vs Tehran's ‘not tomorrow’. Meanwhile the campaign kept moving: the IRGC claims two more supertankers mined (unverified), UKMTO logs attacks off Saudi Arabia and a foiled approach off Yemen, and the WSJ documents Iran's targeting help to the Houthis. Markets closed — no FX moved. Sunday is the double tripwire: the claimed signing and the Graham Act's Oct-18 trigger. Oil's Sunday open (~5pm CT) prices it first.

chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: Saturday's wire split into two tracks: Trump's social-media claim that an Iran deal gets signed Sunday and ‘the Hormuz Strait is OPEN TO ALL’ — vs Tehran saying the signing ‘will not be tomorrow’. Markets closed; the dollar carries the weekend as a risk two-sided bet. Rates unchanged: October locked as a hold (~85%) into the blackout.
chapters.meaning: What changed: Trump's Saturday social posts — the deal is ‘largely negotiated’, signing ‘tomorrow’ (Sunday), the strait ‘OPEN TO ALL’ immediately after — with Pakistan's Sharif prepping an electronic signing. Met Tehran's flat denial: the foreign ministry spokesman said the signing ‘will not be tomorrow’ (though ‘in the coming days cannot be ruled out’), and Fars called Trump's claim ‘inconsistent with reality’. The four-beat read on the claim: (1) it's a social-media post, not a signature — no text, no countersignature, nothing on paper; (2) the surprise is the specificity — a Sunday date plus a mediator prepping e-signature carries more weight than the usual ‘deal imminent’ cycle, and Araghchi himself echoed signing expectations Friday; (3) against the benchmark of this war's repeated near-deals that died at exactly this point, the prior is walk-back — but the mediator prep is the one new ingredient; (4) for the dollar, a real Sunday signing unwinds the haven bid (DXY fades toward 101.3); another walk-back re-arms it (102.2 back in play). The one-question lens: Sunday night, do tankers move or do posts get walked back? Thread: Friday's edition said October was locked as a hold (~85%) with December the debate, and Saturday added nothing on rates — the blackout holds. What it means: the rate thesis is untouched; the weekend's live wire is the risk track, and it's genuinely two-sided. The dollar's Sunday is binary — signing vs walk-back — and oil's Sunday open (~5pm CT) prices it before FX can.
chapters.fx: What to watch: Sunday — the claimed signing (Tehran says ‘not tomorrow’) vs the Graham Act's Oct-18 tripwire (enforcement vs waiver extension); oil's Sunday open ~5pm CT as the first price on all of it; the blackout continues — no Fed voices until Oct 27-28.

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Saturday added four incidents and one claim to the campaign ledger: the IRGC says two supertankers hit mines in Hormuz (no independent confirmation), UKMTO logs two tankers attacked off Saudi Arabia Friday and a foiled skiff approach on an LNG tanker off Yemen — plus the WSJ documenting Iran's targeting help to the Houthis, and Trump's Sunday-signing claim vs Tehran's denial. WTI $100.71 / Brent $109.28 Friday; Sunday open ~5pm CT prices it all.
chapters.meaning: What changed: five Saturday items. (1) The IRGC (via IRNA) claims two oil tankers carrying ~2 million barrels caught fire after hitting naval mines in Hormuz Saturday, having ‘switched off positioning and radar’ on an unauthorised route — Reuters carried it with ‘no independent confirmation’. Still single-attribution, still not in the price (the claim the morning edition held out). (2) UKMTO: two tankers attacked off Saudi Arabia Friday — one projectile strike, one RPG fire, damage to the aft port quarter. (3) UKMTO Saturday: an LNG tanker 140nm southeast of Yemen's Al Mukalla approached by a 7-person skiff that fired two shots; the ship's armed security fired two warning shots and repelled it — no damage, no casualties, a foiled approach, not a strike. (4) The WSJ: Iran is giving the Houthis targeting and intelligence for attacks on Saudi Arabia — ‘the connection is very, very strong on the operational level’ — with the Houthis now controlling the Bab el-Mandeb coastline, a second chokepoint for Saudi oil exports. (5) Trump's Sunday-signing claim vs Tehran's denial (USD chapter). Thread: Friday's edition said the campaign was broadening (MT ST 3 confirmed in Hormuz, YARA J drone-hit off Romania) while diplomacy stretched (‘more time’, Vienna technical talks next week). What it means: confirms and extends geographically — the Yemen/Bab el-Mandeb axis is now an active second front for Saudi oil exports, not just Hormuz. But Saturday also produced the first concrete off-ramp test of the war: a dated Sunday signing claim with a mediator prepping e-signature. The ~$10.7 spread read stands from Friday: (1) it's what the world pays over the US price for seaborne crude; (2) near the wide end — the premium for shipping risk; (3) a wide spread means the market prices tankers, not demand — the risk lives in the strait; (4) for FX, the spread is the CAD-vs-JPY/EUR tell in one number — wide favors the exporter, taxes the importers. Held, not priced: the IRGC mine claims stay single-attribution — one named vessel was the bar Friday (MT ST 3), and these have no names and no UKMTO confirmation.
chapters.fx: What to watch: Sunday — the claimed signing (Tehran: ‘not tomorrow’) vs the Graham Act's Oct-18 tripwire on Russian-oil buyers; oil's Sunday open ~5pm CT; any verified new Hormuz/Bab el-Mandeb incident; Vienna technical talks next week.
